business.title: Object groups mutually bias each other’s perceived average size, as evidenced by neural and behavioural data
business.desc: The human visual system simultaneously computes summary statistics of object features, such as average size, across groups of objects. Evidence suggests that summary statistics across groups of objects (ensembles) are not independent but influence one another. We investigated whether an ensemble’s average size affects the perceived average size of another ensemble, and whether such changes are reflected in altered activation patterns in the visual cortex. Distractor ensembles’ average sizes altered the perceived average size of target ensembles in a contrast-like manner: Large distractor ensembles decreased the target ensembles’ perceived average sizes; conversely, smaller distractor ensembles increased target ensembles’ perceived average sizes. These contrast effects were reflected in more activated voxels in retinotopic regions when target ensembles were perceived as larger. Distractor ensembles’ voxel counts were similarly modulated by target ensembles’ average size, suggesting their perceived average size was also altered. Additionally, individual differences in the magnitude of the ensemble-size contrast effect covaried with activation in higher-level regions, including the left intraparietal sulcus (IPS) and middle temporal gyrus (MTG). Together, these findings suggest that ensemble summary statistics are contrasted, resulting in changes in perceived size and altered retinotopic activation pattern, with involvement of a network including left IPS and left MTG.

business.title: A robust resilience improvement method for distribution network based on pre-layout and dynamic scheduling of grid-forming mobile energy storage
business.desc: To enhance the resilience of distribution networks (DN) against extreme disasters, this paper proposes a robust resilience improvement method based on the pre-layout and dynamic scheduling of grid-forming mobile energy storage (GF-MES). The method follows a pre-disaster defense (PD) and post-disaster recovery (PR) framework. In the PD phase, a two-stage robust optimization (TS-RO) model is formulated considering PV output uncertainty, aiming to optimize both investment costs and load curtailment. The Column-and-Constraint Generation (C&CG) algorithm is used to determine the initial GF-MES deployment plan. In the PR phase, by leveraging the capabilities of GF-MES in frequency regulation and power support and integrating changes in the operation status of the traffic network (TN), a power supply recovery (PSR) model is developed to coordinate GF-MES and electric vehicle stations (EVS). This model is solved as a mixed-integer second-order cone problem (MISOCP) to obtain the optimal scheduling strategy. Finally, simulations are conducted on a modified IEEE 69-bus DN, and the simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the resilience of the DN.

business.title: Technical validation and feasibility of video particle tracking for low-volume measurement of biliary micro-viscosity after liver transplantation
business.desc: Reliable quantification of the biophysical properties of human bile requires analytically validated methods and standardized pre-analytical conditions. We hypothesized that biliary micro-viscosity can be quantified in human bile after liver transplantation (LTx) with predefined analytical performance (accuracy $$\le 15\%$$ deviation from reference, reproducibility CV $$<10\%$$ ). In this method-development and technical-validation study, we established a method to quantify micro-viscosity in human bile after LTx. Validation using sucrose standards demonstrated high accuracy ( $$\le 15\%$$ deviation from reference), strong linear correlation ( $$\textrm{R}^2 = 0.996$$ ), and good reproducibility (CV $$<10\%$$ ). The method was applied to 21 bile samples from nine patients collected longitudinally after LTx. Mean micro-viscosity was $$1.58 \pm 0.54~\text {mPa s}$$ (postoperative day 1), $$1.94 \pm 0.63~\text {mPa s}$$ (day 7), and $$1.44 \pm 0.16~\text {mPa s}$$ (day 14). Pre-analytical freezing and cooling introduced measurement variability, supporting analysis shortly after collection. These findings demonstrate the analytical performance and practical feasibility of video particle-tracking-based biliary micro-viscosity measurements after LTx. Larger studies combining standardized fresh-sample workflows, biochemical bile characterization, and longitudinal clinical outcome data are required to determine the biological relevance of biliary micro-viscosity and its potential value for future graft modeling.

technology.title: HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
technology.desc: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions. Authors show in 2013-2023 France saw a substantial reduction in hepatitis C virus prevalence and incidence among people who use drugs. Widespread treatment and harm reduction drove the decline, bringing France closer to WHO 2030 elimination targets.

technology.title: Why You Shouldn’t Rush to Uninstall Your Genuine Licensed Copy
technology.desc: The rapid advancement of AI coding technologies is fundamentally reshaping developers’ and tech industry practitioners’ perceptions of software development completion standards. Unlike the traditional coding paradigm that defines "degree of completion" solely by full manual implementation of all functional modules, AI-powered coding tools — including intelligent code generation assistants, automated bug detection systems, and AI-driven code optimization platforms — have redefined the benchmarks for measuring development maturity: a high-completion software product no longer requires 100% hand-coded lines, but emphasizes the seamless integration of AI-generated snippets, rigorous functional validation, robust performance output, and compliant maintainable architecture. This shift not only breaks the long-standing stereotype that equates "high completion" with massive manual coding workload, but also drives the global software development ecosystem to establish more efficient, AI-centric evaluation frameworks for development deliverables.
